newsitem.title: NORWAY: Nordics say would back Brundtland as Annan deputy.
newsitem.headline: Nordics say would back Brundtland as Annan deputy.

text.p: Nordic foreign ministers said on Wednesday they would like to see former Norwegian prime minister Gro Harlem Brundtland get a job at the United Nations or elsewhere in international diplomacy.
The ministers were commenting on a report in the Norwegian daily newspaper Arbeiderbladet which said that Brundtland had been asked by the U.N.'s new secretary-general, Kofi Annan, to be his deputy.
It quoted diplomatic sources at the United Nations as saying Annan made the offer to Brundtland during a meeting in New York on January 10, and that she had not yet replied.

"We all highly respect Gro Harlem Brundtland," Swedish Foreign Minister Lena Hjelm-Wallen said. "I am sure that there would be Nordic backing regardless of which international position we are talking about. But formally, the question has not come up."
She was responding to a question at a joint news conference with her four Nordic colleagues, who were holding a regular meeting in Oslo.
Danish Foreign Minister Niels Helveg Petersen concurred, adding: "I would like to see the World Health Organisation (WHO) getting a new and strong leadership."
Arbeiderbladet, which has close relations with Norway's ruling Labour party, of which Brundtland is a member, said she was also favoured to land a top job at the Geneva-based WHO this year.
"If she goes for this job Kofi Annan would no doubt support her," the report said. "But he would rather see her move to New York than to Geneva."

Brundtland, a medical doctor by training, resigned last October after dominating Norwegian politics for more than a decade. Citing family reasons, she subsequently declared she would also quit parliament this year.
She has always refused comment on long-standing speculation she might leave Norway for an international position.
Brundtland, 57, who is writing a book about her three terms as premier, has been mentioned in the past as a possible candidate for the job of U.N. secretary-general or NATO secretary-general.
She has enjoyed international recognition since 1983 as chairwoman of the U.N. World Commission on Environment and Development and is also known as a champion of women's issues.
